findings.heading: Slicing
findings.proposition: The English NOTE says top_n() has been superseded BY the slice functions; the Turkish says 'slice islevlerinin yerini alan top_n()', i.e. top_n() takes the place of the slice functions, reversing which function is deprecated.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader concludes top_n() is the current replacement for slice_max()/slice_min() and writes new code with a superseded dplyr function, contradicting the whole surrounding section.

findings.heading: Probabilistic de-duplication
findings.proposition: The English points the reader to the Joining data page with a working link target, [Joining data](joining_matching.qmd); the Turkish writes '[Verileri birlestirme]' with no link target at all, so the cross-reference to the chapter that explains probabilistic matching is absent.
findings.reader_consequence: The only explanation of the probabilistic de-duplication method lives in another chapter. The Turkish reader sees literal bracket text instead of a link and cannot reach that explanation from here.

findings.heading: Keep all but mark them
findings.proposition: The English recommends 'consider a two-step approach utilizing a unique recordID/encounter number'; the Turkish sentence drops the whole 'consider a two-step approach utilizing' clause and ends on the bare fragment 'benzersiz bir recordID/encounter number:'.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader gets a verbless fragment that never states the recommended method. The two numbered steps that follow arrive with no statement that they form the recommended two-step approach built on a unique record identifier.

findings.heading: Examine duplicate rows
findings.proposition: The English says rows with the same values in the 'name' and 'purpose' columns are returned; the Turkish glosses the second column as 'amac - `name`', naming the column `name` twice, while the chunk beside it calls janitor::get_dupes(name, purpose).
findings.reader_consequence: A reader matching the prose to the code sees `name` given as the identifier for the purpose column and can conclude get_dupes() was called on `name` alone, which does not explain why amrish has dupe_count 3 for his three 'contact' encounters.

findings.heading: Slice with groups
findings.proposition: The English states the outcome of setting with_ties = FALSE: 'We get back only one row per person.' The Turkish paragraph ends after 'Bunu onlemek icin with_ties = FALSE olarak ayarladik.' and never states that outcome.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader is told the setting avoids the problem but is never told the resulting guarantee of exactly one row per person, which is the point of the de-duplication step and the basis for reading the table that follows.

findings.heading: Calculate row completeness
findings.proposition: The English says `.` within piping refers to the data frame at that point in the pipe; the Turkish says `.` refers to 'veri cercevesindeki bir nokta', i.e. a point inside the data frame, which is not what the pipe placeholder denotes.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader misunderstands the `.` placeholder used in rowSums(!is.na(.[,key_cols])) as pointing at a location within the data, not at the piped data frame itself, and cannot transfer the idiom to their own pipes.

findings.heading: Load packages
findings.proposition: The English says p_load() 'installs the package if necessary *and* loads it for use'; the Turkish moves the condition to the loading step ('paketi kuran *ve* eger gerekirse kullanim icin yukleyen'), so it claims installation is unconditional and loading is conditional.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader can conclude p_load() reinstalls a package on every run, and may avoid it in favour of library() to prevent an unwanted reinstall.

findings.heading: Roll-up values into one row
findings.proposition: The comment beside ~paste0(na.omit(.x), collapse = '; ') says in English that the function combines non-NA values; the Turkish says it combines 'NA olmayan benzersiz degerleri' (unique non-NA values), although this chunk contains no unique() call.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish comment is identical to the one on the unique() variation (tr lines 533 and 543), so the reader loses the contrast the section is built on and expects the first roll-up to drop repeated values when it keeps every one of them. The same wrong comment repeats at tr line 516.
